subject: agriculture
topicTitle: Soil Science, Fertilizers, Irrigation, Agronomy of Major Crops
thirtySecondSummary: Soil science investigates soil genesis, profile horizons (O, A, B, C), physical properties (texture, structure, bulk density 1.33 g/cm³, particle density 2.65 g/cm³), and soil reactions (acid, saline, sodic).

Essential plant nutrients (17 elements, Arnon & Stout criteria) are categorized into Basic (C, H, O), Primary (N, P, K), Secondary (Ca, Mg, S), and Micronutrients (Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl, Ni); Nickel was added as the 17th essential element.

Commercial fertilizers supply concentrated nutrients: Urea (46% N), DAP (18% N, 46% P2O5), MOP (60% K2O), and SSP (16% P2O5, 11% S, 19% Ca); Biofertilizers include Rhizobium (legumes), Azotobacter (free-living), and VAM (phosphorus uptake).

Irrigation scheduling targets critical growth stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI at 20-25 DAS) in wheat; Panicle initiation & flowering in rice. Advanced pressurized methods include Drip irrigation (90-95% water use efficiency) and Sprinkler systems.
Agronomy of major crops encompasses seed rates, spacing, weed control, and fertilizer regimes for Cereals (Rice, Wheat, Maize), Pulses (Chickpea, Pigeonpea), and Oilseeds (Mustard, Groundnut).

coreConcepts.title: Soil Physical Properties, Chemistry and Problematic Soils
coreConcepts.explanation:
Soil is a dynamic natural body comprising mineral matter (45%), organic matter (5%), water (25%), and air (25%).
1. Physical Properties: Texture (relative proportion of sand, silt, and clay; cannot be changed by farmers); Structure (arrangement of primary soil particles into peds/aggregates; crumb/granular structure is best for crops); Bulk Density (mass of dry soil per unit total volume, typical range 1.2-1.6 g/cm³; particle density is ~2.65 g/cm³).
2. Problematic Soils & Reclamation:
- Acid Soils (pH < 6.5): High Al, Fe, and Mn toxicity, deficient in P and Ca; reclaimed by applying Agricultural Lime (CaCO3).
- Saline Soils (Solonchak, Electrical Conductivity EC > 4 dS/m, Exchangeable Sodium Percentage ESP < 15, pH < 8.5): Reclaimed by leaching with good quality water and installing drainage.
- Sodic / Alkali Soils (Solonetz, EC < 4 dS/m, ESP > 15, pH > 8.5): Dispersed structure due to high Na+; reclaimed by applying Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O), replacing exchangeable Na+ with Ca2+.
keyTakeaways: Soil composition: 45% mineral, 5% organic, 25% water, 25% air.
Saline soil reclamation: Leaching with drainage.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit III, Soil Science section, pp. 95-108.

coreConcepts.title: Plant Nutrition, Fertilizers, and Biofertilizers
coreConcepts.explanation:
Arnon & Stout (1939) established criteria of essentiality: a plant cannot complete its life cycle without the element, its action is specific, and it is directly involved in metabolism.
1. Classification:
- Primary: Nitrogen (vegetative growth, protein), Phosphorus ('key to life', root development, ATP), Potassium (enzyme activation, stomatal regulation, disease resistance).
- Secondary: Calcium (cell wall pectin), Magnesium (central atom of chlorophyll ring), Sulfur (amino acids methionine and cysteine).
- Micronutrients: Fe, Mn, Zn ('Khaira' disease in rice), Cu, B (pollen germination, fruit cracking), Mo (nitrogenase enzyme cofactor), Cl, Ni (urease cofactor).
2. Commercial Fertilizers:
- Urea: 46% N (highest among solid N fertilizers).
- Diammonium Phosphate (DAP): 18% N and 46% P2O5.
- Muriate of Potash (MOP / KCl): 60% K2O.
- Single Super Phosphate (SSP): 16% P2O5, 11-12% Sulfur, 19% Calcium.
3. Biofertilizers: Rhizobium (symbiotic N-fixation with legumes; e.g., R. leguminosarum, R. japonicum); Azotobacter (free-living aerobic N-fixer in wheat/maize); Azospirillum (associative N-fixer in sorghum/millets); Blue Green Algae (BGA) and Azolla-Anabaena (lowland wetland rice); Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza (VAM, mobilize insoluble phosphorus).
keyTakeaways: Fertilizer grades: Urea = 46% N; DAP = 18-46-0; MOP = 60% K2O; SSP = 16% P2O5 + 11% S.
Khaira disease of rice: Zinc deficiency; rectified with ZnSO4 spray.
Rhizobium: Symbiotic N-fixation in pulses; VAM: Phosphorus mobilizer.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit III, Fertilizers & Nutrition, pp. 110-124.

coreConcepts.title: Irrigation Methods and Agronomy of Major Field Crops
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. Water Management & Critical Stages:
- Wheat: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) at 20-25 days after sowing (DAS) is the most critical stage; skipping irrigation here reduces yield by > 30%.
- Rice: Panicle initiation, flowering, and milk stages require continuous shallow submergence (5 cm).
- Advanced Methods: Drip / Trickle irrigation delivers water drop-by-drop to the root zone (efficiency 90-95%, ideal for orchards, row crops, water-scarce regions); Sprinkler irrigation (efficiency 75-80%, ideal for undulating sandy soils, unsuited for windy or heavy clay soils).
2. Agronomy of Key Crops:
- Rice (Oryza sativa): Seed rate: Direct seeded 80-100 kg/ha; Transplanted 40-50 kg/ha; Dapog method 1.5-3 kg/m² nursery (seedlings ready in 11-14 days); SRI (System of Rice Intensification) 5 kg/ha (seedlings at 8-12 days).
- Wheat (Triticum aestivum): Seed rate 100 kg/ha (normal), 125 kg/ha (late sown); Spacing 22.5 x 5 cm; Dominant weed Phalaris minor (Canary grass, managed with Clodinafop / Sulfosulfuron).
- Chickpea (Cicer arietinum): Desi (seed rate 65-75 kg/ha) vs Kabuli (100 kg/ha); Nipping at 30-40 DAS to promote lateral branching; susceptible to pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera).
keyTakeaways: Most critical stage in Wheat: Crown Root Initiation (CRI at 20-25 DAS).
Dapog method in rice: Seedlings ready in 11-14 days without soil contact.
SRI technique: 25 x 25 cm spacing, single young seedling (8-12 days old), 5 kg seed/ha.
Canary grass (Phalaris minor): Mimic weed of wheat controlled by Sulfosulfuron.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit III, Agronomy of Crops, pp. 126-143.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Occurs at 20-25 days after sowing (DAS) in wheat
keyFacts.explanation: Transitional phase where seminal roots give way to permanent crown roots; moisture stress here drastically halts tillering.
keyFacts.examTip: If only one irrigation is available for wheat, it must be applied at CRI stage.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Deficiency of Zinc (Zn) | Discovered by Y.L. Nene at Pantnagar (1966)
keyFacts.explanation: Symptoms: Chlorosis of younger leaves followed by rusty brown spots on older leaves; cured by foliar spray of 0.5% ZnSO4 + 0.25% Lime.
keyFacts.examTip: Frequently tested mineral deficiency symptom in CUET.

keyFacts.explanation: Calcium ions replace sodium ions from clay exchange complexes, forming soluble sodium sulfate that is leached out with water.
keyFacts.examTip: Contrast with acid soils which need lime (CaCO3).

keyFacts.explanation: Ideal phosphorus source for oilseeds and pulses due to its high sulfur content.
keyFacts.examTip: CUET asks which phosphorus fertilizer contains sulfur.

workedExamples.question: If a farmer has access to irrigation water for only ONE single irrigation throughout the entire wheat crop season, at which phenological growth stage must it be applied to avoid catastrophic yield loss?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the critical growth stages of wheat: CRI (20-25 DAS), Tillering (40-45 DAS), Jointing (60-65 DAS), Flowering (80-85 DAS), Milking (100-105 DAS), Dough (115-120 DAS).
Step 2: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) is universally established as the single most critical irrigation stage.
Step 3: Moisture deficit at CRI irreversibly curtails crown root anchoring and tiller proliferation, causing up to 35-40% yield penalty.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: The 'single irrigation priority at CRI' is one of the most repeatedly asked agronomy questions in all agricultural competitive exams.

workedExamples.question: Which chemical amendment is specifically recommended for the chemical reclamation of sodic (alkali) soils having an ESP > 15 and pH > 8.5?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Diagnose the soil type: Sodic (alkali) soils suffer from excess exchangeable sodium on the clay complex.
Step 2: Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) supplies soluble Ca2+ ions.
Step 3: Ca2+ displaces adsorbed Na+, converting sodium clay to calcium clay and forming soluble Na2SO4 which is leached out.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Always remember: Acid soils -> Lime; Sodic/Alkali soils -> Gypsum.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: 'Khaira' disease in rice is caused by the deficiency of which mineral nutrient?
howCuetAsks.strategy: Immediately identify Zinc (Zn) deficiency, discovered by Dr. Y.L. Nene at Pantnagar.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: How much nitrogen is contained in a 50 kg bag of commercial Urea fertilizer?
howCuetAsks.strategy: Urea is 46% N. Therefore, in 50 kg of urea: 50 x 0.46 = 23 kg of Nitrogen.

commonTraps.whyItTraps: Students confuse acidic and alkaline problematic soils. Lime (CaCO3) raises pH and is used for ACID soils; Gypsum (CaSO4) reduces exchangeable sodium without raising pH in SODIC soils.

commonTraps.trap: Confusing Dapog nursery duration with conventional wet nursery in rice.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: Conventional wet bed seedlings take 25-30 days to transplant; Dapog seedlings are ready in just 11-14 days.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Dapog = 11 to 14 days (fastest nursery technique, originating from Philippines).

mnemonics.meaning: Crown Root Initiation occurs at ~21 (20-25) days after sowing in wheat.
mnemonics.application: Never forget the exact DAS for CRI stage in wheat.

practiceQuestions.question: The percentage of elemental nitrogen contained in commercial technical-grade Urea fertilizer is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Urea (CO(NH2)2) contains 46% Nitrogen, the highest nitrogen content among dry solid nitrogenous fertilizers.

practiceQuestions.question: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage in wheat normally occurs at how many days after sowing (DAS)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) occurs 20 to 25 days after sowing and marks the critical initiation of the secondary root system in wheat.

practiceQuestions.question: Which major crop deficiency disorder is characterized by rusty brown patches on rice leaves and is caused by the lack of Zinc?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Khaira disease of rice is an abiotic physiological disorder resulting from zinc deficiency in calcareous or waterlogged soils.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Drip irrigation achieves the highest water use efficiency (90-95%) among all irrigation methods.
Reason (R): Water is applied directly and precisely to the plant root zone drop-by-drop at low rates, virtually eliminating surface evaporation and deep percolation losses.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are factually accurate and (R) provides the exact physiological and hydraulic mechanism explaining why drip irrigation achieves 90-95% efficiency.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Fertilizer) with List-II (Primary Nutrient Content):
List-I:
(P) Urea
(Q) DAP
(R) MOP
(S) Single Super Phosphate

List-II:
(1) 60% K2O
(2) 46% N
(3) 16% P2O5
(4) 18% N and 46% P2O5
practiceQuestions.explanation: Urea = 46% N; DAP = 18% N & 46% P2O5; MOP = 60% K2O; SSP = 16% P2O5.

practiceQuestions.question: In the 'Dapog' method of raising rice seedlings originating from the Philippines, seedlings become ready for field transplanting in how many days?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In the Dapog nursery raised on non-absorbent surfaces like polythene or banana leaves, seedlings draw nutrition purely from the endosperm and are ready for transplanting within 11 to 14 days.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is an obnoxious canary grass weed that mimics wheat morphologically, posing serious control challenges?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Phalaris minor (locally known as Gulli Danda or Mandusi) is a notorious mimic weed in irrigated wheat fields.

practiceQuestions.question: Which symbiotic biofertilizer organism forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules exclusively in leguminous pulse crops?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Rhizobium species form an obligate symbiotic relationship with leguminous roots, establishing bacteroid nodules containing leghemoglobin that fix atmospheric N2.

practiceQuestions.question: The chemical compound Agricultural Gypsum used to reclaim alkali soils has the chemical formula:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate (CaSO4.2H2O), supplying soluble calcium to displace toxic sodium from clay exchange complexes.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the recommended seed rate of rice under the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) technique?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The SRI technique utilizes only 5 kg of seed per hectare because single young seedlings (8-12 days old) are transplanted at wide square spacing (25 x 25 cm).
